en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.6. Saṅkiliṭṭhattika (The Triplet of the Corrupted)
Section on Analysis:
The Cause.
Dependent on a defiled and corruptible state, a defiled and corruptible state arises by way of the cause-condition—namely, a defiled and corruptible [state].
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates arise … dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on a defiled and defiling state, a non-defiled but defiling state arises by way of root condition: dependent on defiled and defiling aggregates, mind-produced matter arises.
Dependent on a defiled and defiling state, both a defiled and defiling state and a non-defiled but defiling state arise … [and so forth].

And states arise with a root-condition: dependent on one defiled and defiling aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Dependent on a state that is not defiled but defiling, a state that is not defiled but defiling arises.

By way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate that is not defiled but subject to defilement, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter;
at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate that is not defiled but subject to defilement, there arise three aggregates and kamma-produced matter … [and so forth].

Dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and derived matter produced by kamma; dependent on the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base; dependent on the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates;
dependent on one great primary, there arise three great primaries …pe… dependent on the great primaries, there arise mind-produced matter, matter produced by kamma, and derived matter.
Dependent on a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement, a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement, three aggregates arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.

Dependent on a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement, a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement arises by way of root condition: dependent on aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement, mind-produced matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement, states that are both undefiled but subject to defilement and neither defiled nor subject to defilement arise by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement...
Three aggregates and mind-produced matter …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.

Dependent on a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement and a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement, a state that is defiled but not subject to defilement arises by way of root condition:
dependent on aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement and the great elements.
Matter produced by mind.

Dependent on states that are both defiled and subject to defilement (*saṅkiliṭṭha-saṅkilesika*) and states that are undefiled but subject to defilement (*asaṅkiliṭṭha-saṅkilesika*), an undefiled but defiled state arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*):
dependent on aggregates that are both defiled and subject to defilement and the great elements (*mahābhūta*).
Matter originated by mind. (Abbreviated.
Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.

In the case of root-cause condition, nine; object condition, three; predominance condition, nine; proximity condition, three; contiguity condition, three; conascence condition, nine; mutuality condition, three;
dependence condition, nine; strong-dependence condition, three; prenascence condition, three; repetition condition, three;
kamma condition, nine; resultant condition, five; nutriment condition, nine …pe… path condition, nine; association condition, three; dissociation condition …pe… [nine].
Nine ... pe ... nine non-disappearance conditions. (Abbreviated.
(It should be analyzed in the same manner as it was analyzed in the *Kusala-ttika*. 1.6.1.2.
Negative Conditions (*Paccaya-paccanīya*)
Vibhaṅgavāra: Non-root Condition.
Dependent on a defiled and corruptible state, there arises a defiled and corruptible state by way of the non-root condition—[namely,] that which is accompanied by doubt.
In dependence on aggregates accompanied by restlessness, arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
In dependence on a state that is not defiled but subject to defilement, a state that is not defiled but subject to defilement arises by way of the not-root condition:
in dependence on one rootless aggregate that is not defiled but subject to defilement, three aggregates [arise].
And mind-originated matter ... [etc. ... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking ... [etc. ... one great primary of non-percipient beings. (Abbreviated.
It should be analyzed in the same way as it was analyzed in the Wholesome Triplet.
Pure.
With not-root condition, two; with not-object condition, five; with not-predominance condition, six; with not-proximity condition, five …pe… with not-strong-dependence condition, five;
with not-prenascence condition, seven; with not-postnascence condition, nine; with not-repetition condition, nine; with not-kamma condition, three; with not-resultant condition, nine;

with not-nutriment condition, one …pe… with not-path condition, one; with not-association condition, five; with not-dissociation condition, three; with not-absence condition …pe… [same as not-presence].
Five [factors] are not dissociated; five [factors] are not dissociated. (Abbreviated.
1.6.1.3. Positive-Negative Conditionality:
The Root-Duad.
With root condition, there are five [instances] where there is no object condition; six where there is no predominance condition ... pe ... seven where there is no prenascence condition;

nine where there is no postnascence condition; nine where there is no repetition condition; three where there is no kamma condition; nine where there is no result condition; five where there is no association condition;
three where there is no dissociation condition; five where there is no absence condition; five where there is no disappearance condition. (Abbreviated.)
1.6.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma) The Non-root Pair (Nahetuduka):

With the non-root condition, there are two [types of relations] with the object condition … pe … one with the result condition … pe … one with the path condition … pe … two with the non-disappearance condition. (Abbreviated.)
The Section on Dependence (Paṭiccavāra).

1.6.2–6. The Chapter on Co-nascence Condition, Support, Conjoined, and Associated (The Chapter on Co-nascence, the Chapter on Conditions, the Chapter on Support, the Chapter on Conjoined, and the Chapter on Associated are to be expanded in detail).
1.6.7. Chapter on Questions (Pañhāvāra) 1.6.7.1.
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra): Positive Conditionality (Paccayānuloma)

A defiled and corruptible state is a condition for a defiled and corruptible state by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*): defiled and corruptible roots are a condition for their associated aggregates by way of the root-condition.

A defiled and corruptible state is a condition for a non-defiled but corruptible state by way of the root-condition: defiled and corruptible roots are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the root-condition.
A defiled and corruptible state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for both a defiled and corruptible state and an undefiled but corruptible state:
defiled and corruptible roots are a root-condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A not-defiled-and-defiling state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a not-defiled-and-defiling state:
not-defiled-and-defiling roots are a condition, by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter;
at the moment of rebirth-linking, not-defiled-and-defiling roots [are a condition] for their associated [aggregates].
The aggregates and the matter produced by them (kaṭattā-rūpa) are related to [their own] aggregates by way of root-condition.

A non-defiled and non-defiling state is related to a non-defiled and non-defiling state by way of root-condition: non-defiled and non-defiling roots are related to their associated aggregates by way of root-condition.

A non-defiled and non-defiling state is related to a non-defiled and defiling state by way of root-condition: non-defiled and non-defiling roots are related to mind-produced matter by way of root-condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is both defiled and subject to defilement, and for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement: roots that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are a condition,
by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
An object that is defiled and subject to defilement is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is defiled and subject to defilement:
one relishes and delights in lust; with that as object, lust arises, and wrong view arises.
Doubt arises, restlessness arises, and grief arises.

One relishes wrong view … [and so on] … based on doubt … based on restlessness … based on grief … It should be analyzed in the same way as it was explained in the *Kusalattika* (The Triplet of the Wholesome).
A defiled and corrupting state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not defiled but is corrupting:
noble ones review abandoned defilements; they review suppressed defilements;
they know previously practiced defilements; [they contemplate] the defiled and corrupting aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
They see with insight; through the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, they know the mind of one possessing a defiled and corruptible mind.
Or, whether they be trainees (sekkhā) or worldlings (puthujjana), they see the defiled and corruptible aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
When the wholesome [state] has ceased, the resultant [consciousness] arises as its object; [they likewise see] the defiled and corruptible...
They relish and delight in the aggregates... [as above] ...grief arises; when unwholesome states have ceased, their resultant arises with them as its object.

Defiled and defiling aggregates are related to knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of recollection of past lives, knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds, knowledge of future existences, and to advertence, by way of object-condition.
A state that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption:
having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, or having performed the Uposatha rite, one reviews it;
one reviews former good deeds; having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna; the Noble Ones review the change-of-lineage (gotrabhu).
They review it; they review purification; they practice insight into the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;

[they practice insight into] the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical basis [of consciousness] … they practice insight into the aggregates, which are not defiled but subject to defilement, as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; with the divine eye...

They see forms; they hear sounds with the divine ear-element; by means of the knowledge of penetration of minds, they know the mind of one possessing a mind that is undefiled yet subject to defilement.

The base of infinite space is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the base of infinite consciousness... [and so on] ...the base of nothingness is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
The sense-sphere of visible form is a condition, by way of object-condition, for eye-consciousness.
...pe... the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of object-condition.

Non-defiled-but-not-purifying aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of the modes of psychic power, the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds, the knowledge of future existences, and for advertence, by way of object-condition.
A not-defiled-and-defiling state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a defiled-and-defiling state:
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, or performed an observance-day duty, one relishes and delights in it;
taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises ... pe ... grief arises; [or] formerly well-performed deeds ...
One relishes [the jhāna] … having emerged from jhāna, one relishes the jhāna … one relishes the eye.
One relishes and delights in tangible objects … the physical basis … and the undefiled-but-favourable-to-defilement aggregates;
taking them as an object, lust arises … grief arises.

An undefiled and non-defiling state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an undefiled and non-defiling state: Nibbāna is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the Path and the Fruition.
An undefiled and non-defiling state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a defiled but undefiled state:
the Noble Ones, having emerged from the Path, review the Path, review the Fruition, [and review] Nibbāna.
They review it. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū), purification (vodāna), and adverting (āvajjanā) by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya).
Noble ones, by means of the knowledge of penetration of minds (cetopariyañāṇa), know the mind of one possessing a mind that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement.

The aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are [conditions] for the knowledge of penetration of minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives (pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa), the knowledge of future states (anāgataṁsañāṇa), and adverting.
It is a condition by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya).
A defiled and defiling state is a condition for a defiled and defiling state by way of predominance-condition (adhipatipaccaya).
Condition: object-predominance and conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: Taking lust as estimable, one relishes it and delights in it;
taking that as estimable, lust arises and wrong view arises. Taking wrong view as estimable, one relishes it and delights in it;
taking that as estimable, lust arises and wrong view arises. Conascence-predominance: the predominance of the defiled and subject to defilement.
It is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
A defiled and corruptible state is a condition for a non-defiled but corruptible state by way of predominance-condition.
As co-nascent predominance: a defiled and corruptible predominance is a condition for mind-produced matter.
Condition by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

A defiled and corrupting state is a condition by way of predominance condition for both a defiled and corrupting state and a non-defiled but corrupting state. Conascent predominance: defiled and corrupting predominance.
It is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

A state that is neither-defiled-nor-obsessed (*asaṅkiliṭṭha-saṅkilesika*) is a condition for a state that is neither-defiled-nor-obsessed by way of predominance condition—namely, object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*).
Object-predominance: having given a gift, having undertaken moral discipline...
Having performed the Uposatha ritual, one esteems it and reviews it; having esteemed previously well-performed deeds, one reviews them;
having emerged from jhāna, one esteems the jhāna and reviews it; those in training (sekkhā) esteem the change-of-lineage (gotrabhu) and review it;
they esteem purification (vodāna) and review it. Co-nascent predominance (sahajātādhipati): non-defiled-but-defiling predominance.
It is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
A non-defiled-but-defiling state is a condition for a defiled-and-defiling state by way of the predominance condition. As object-predominance:
having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, or having performed the Uposatha duty, one [reflects upon it...]
One esteems, relishes, and delights in it; esteeming it, lust arises and wrong view arises.
One esteems, relishes, and delights in past deeds well-performed... Having emerged from jhāna, one esteems, relishes, and delights in the jhāna...
One esteems, relishes, and delights in the eye... [and so on] ...in tangible objects.
... [as before] ... Regarding the bases as not defiled but subject to defilement, one esteems, relishes, and delights in the aggregates;
esteeming them, lust arises and wrong view arises.
A state that is not defiled and not subject to defilement is a condition for a state that is not defiled and not subject to defilement by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
Condition: object-predominance and conascent-predominance. Object-predominance: Nibbāna is a condition for the path and the fruit by way of predominance-condition.
Conascent-predominance: An unpolluted and non-polluting predominance is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of predominance-condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement—namely, object-predominance and conascence-predominance. Object-predominance:
Noble ones, having emerged from the Path, esteem and review the Path; they esteem and review the Fruit; they esteem [and review] Nibbāna...
Having done so, they review it; Nibbāna is related to change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) and purification (vodāna) by way of predominance condition (adhipatipaccaya).
Co-nascent predominance (sahajātādhipati): a predominance that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling is related to mind-produced matter by way of predominance condition.
A state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling is related to a state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling and [a state] that is not-defiled-but-defiling...
And it is a condition for the Dhamma by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*):
an unpolluted and non-polluting predominance is a condition by way of the predominance condition for its associated aggregates (*khandha*) and for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*).
Immediate (*anantara*)...
A defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a defiled and corrupting state by way of proximity-condition:
preceding defiled and corrupting aggregates are a condition for succeeding defiled and corrupting aggregates by way of proximity-condition.

A defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a non-defiled and corrupting state by way of proximity condition: the defiled and corrupting aggregates are a condition for emergence by way of proximity condition.
A non-defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a non-defiled and corrupting state by way of proximity condition:
preceding non-defiled and corrupting aggregates are a condition for succeeding non-defiled and corrupting [aggregates] by way of proximity condition.

[The preceding] aggregates are related to [the succeeding ones] by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*). Adaptation (*anuloma*) is related to change-of-lineage (*gotrabhu*) ... adaptation is related to purification (*vodāna*) ...
advertence (*āvajjanā*) is related to the non-defiled-yet-defiling aggregates by way of proximity condition.
A non-defiled-yet-defiling state is related to a defiled-yet-defiling state by way of proximity condition—advertence is related to the defiled-yet-defiling aggregates by way of proximity condition.
A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is related to a state that is undefiled and not subject to defilement by way of proximity-condition:
change-of-lineage to the path; purification to the path; adaptation to the attainment of fruition;
and for one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related to the attainment of fruition by way of proximity-condition.
A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement:
preceding aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for subsequent aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement.
The path is a condition for the fruit; the fruit is a condition for the fruit by way of proximity-condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement by way of proximity condition: the fruit is a condition for emergence by way of proximity condition.
[The section on] immediate and so forth:
A state that is defiled and subject to defilement is a condition for a state that is defiled and subject to defilement by way of contiguity condition.

Condition …pe… it is a condition by way of co-nascence condition … by way of mutuality condition … by way of support condition … by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive-support, proximity-decisive-support, natural-decisive-support …pe…. Natural-decisive-support:
having relied upon lust, one kills a living being …pe… one causes a schism in the Saṅgha …pe… hatred …pe….

Depending on [something], one kills a living being …pe… causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Lust …pe… aspiration is related to lust …pe… aspiration by way of the decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

Killing a living being is related to killing a living being by way of the decisive support condition …pe… fixed wrong view is related to fixed wrong view by way of the decisive support condition …pe….
A defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a non-defiled but corrupting state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—
namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as above] … Natural decisive support:

relying on lust (*rāga*), one gives a gift, undertakes moral discipline (*sīla*), performs the observance-day duty (*uposathakamma*), [develops] meditative absorption (*jhāna*), insight (*vipassanā*), direct knowledge (*abhiññā*) … [and so forth].
...arouses [it], arouses an attainment (*samāpatti*) ...pe... relying on a wish (*patthana*), one gives a gift ...pe...
arouses an attainment. Greed ...pe... a wish. Faith ...pe... is a condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*) for bodily pleasure and bodily pain.
Having killed a living being, one gives a gift for the sake of warding off that [karma]; morality ...pe... [is likewise].
One undertakes [precepts], performs the Uposatha rite, arouses jhāna, arouses insight, arouses direct knowledge,
arouses meditative attainment …pe… having split the Saṅgha, one gives a gift, undertakes precepts,
and performs the Uposatha rite for the sake of counteracting that [schism]. Unwholesome kamma is a condition for its result by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).

A defiled and corrupting state (*saṅkiliṭṭha-saṅkilesika-dhamma*) is a condition for a state that is undefiled and non-corrupting (*asaṅkiliṭṭha-asaṅkilesika-dhamma*) by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
As natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): relying on lust (*rāga*), one arouses the Path and enters the attainment of fruition (*phalasamāpatti*).
[One relies on] hatred (*dosa*) …pe… and reliance on aspiration (*patthana*), one arouses the Path and enters the attainment of fruition. Lust …pe… [and so forth].
... pe ... aspiration is a condition for the path and for the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling is a condition for a state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support ...

pe ... Natural decisive support: faith ... pe ... *Note: The ellipses indicate that the text continues with the standard list of wholesome qualities (virtue, learning, generosity, etc. as objects of natural decisive support.*
One gives a gift by relying on [a person] … pe … one arouses meditative attainment.

One gives a gift by relying on virtue … learning … generosity … wisdom … bodily pleasure … bodily pain … the climate … food … or a lodging … pe … one arouses meditative attainment. Faith … pe … a lodging is a decisive support for faith … pe … for bodily pleasure.
It is a condition for bodily suffering by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). Wholesome kamma is a condition for its result by way of decisive support condition.
The preparation for the first jhāna is a condition for the first jhāna ... [and so on] ...
the base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception ... [and so on].

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition for a state that is defiled and subject to defilement by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural-decisive support … [as above] … Natural-decisive support:
relying on faith as a decisive support, one arouses conceit and adopts wrong view; relying on virtue … [as above] … or relying on a lodging as a decisive support, one takes life.

It kills … [and so on] … it causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Confidence … [and so on] … lodging is related to lust … [and so on] … to aspiration by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling is related to a state that is undefiled and non-defiling by way of decisive support condition:
as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakata-upanissaya*) … [and so on] …. Natural decisive support: [confidence, etc.,] for the first path.

The preliminary work (*parikamma*) is a condition for the first path by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*) … [and so on] … for the second path … for the third path … for the fourth path.
A state that is undefiled and non-defiling is a condition for a state that is undefiled and non-defiling by way of decisive support condition.
Condition: object-strong-dependence, proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence ... [etc. ... Natural strong-dependence:

the first path is a condition for the second path by way of strong-dependence condition; ... the second path is a condition for the third path; ... the third path is a condition for the fourth path; ...
the path is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of strong-dependence condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement—namely, as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support … [as follows]. Natural decisive support:
Noble ones, relying on the Path as a decisive support, produce an unarisen attainment and enter an arisen attainment.
They practice insight into volitional formations as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.

The Path is related to the Noble Ones’ analytical knowledge of meaning …pe… and to skill in [discerning] what is possible and impossible by way of being a decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya). The attainment of fruition is related to bodily pleasure by way of being a decisive support condition.
A pure, non-defiled, and defiling state is a condition for a pure, non-defiled, and defiling state by way of prenascence condition—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.
Regarding object-prenascence: the eye [is considered] as impermanent, as suffering...

He contemplates as non-self; he contemplates the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical base as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. With the divine eye he sees a visible form;
with the divine ear-element he hears a sound. The visible-form base [is the condition] for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the tangible-base is [the condition] for body-consciousness.
It is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. As basis-pre-nascence: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness ...

[and so on] ... the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. The [heart-]base is a condition for the aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement by way of pre-nascence condition.
A defiled-and-defiling state is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a defiled-and-defiling state:
as object-prenascence and as base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: one relishes and delights in the eye;
taking that as object, lust arises … pe … grief arises. The ear … pe … tangible objects … the [heart-]base.
One relishes it and delights in it; with that as object, lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises. Basis-prenascence:
the physical basis is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for the defiled and defiling aggregates.

A state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling: the physical basis is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for the aggregates that are neither-defiled-nor-defiling.
A subsequently-arisen defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a non-defiled and corrupting state by way of subsequent-arising condition:
subsequently-arisen defiled and corrupting aggregates are a condition for this previously-arisen body by way of subsequent-arising condition.
A state that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption is a condition for a state that is corrupt but not itself corrupt by way of postnascence-condition:
postnascent aggregates that are neither corrupt nor subject to corruption are a condition for this prenascent body by way of postnascence-condition.

A state that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption is a condition for a state that is corrupt but not itself corrupt by way of postnascence-condition... [etc.]... by way of postnascence-condition.
Condition: Postnascent aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are related to this prenascent body by way of postnascence-condition.
Repetition:
A state that is defiled and subject to defilement is related to a state that is defiled and subject to defilement by way of repetition-condition.
Condition: Preceding defiled and defiling aggregates are a condition for subsequent defiled and defiling aggregates by way of repetition-condition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

A non-defiled but defiling state is a condition for a non-defiled but defiling state by way of repetition-condition: preceding [states] ... pe ... adaptation (*anuloma*) is a condition for change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*), and adaptation is a condition for purification (*vodāna*) by way of repetition-condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of repetition-condition (*āsevana-paccaya*), for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement: the change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*) is a condition for the path; purification (*vodāna*) is a condition for the path by way of repetition-condition.
Kamma:

A state that is defiled and subject to defilement is a condition, by way of kamma-condition (*kammapaccaya*), for a state that is defiled and subject to defilement: a volition that is defiled and subject to defilement is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates.
A defiled and defiling state is a condition for a non-defiled but defiling state by way of kamma-condition:

as co-nascent and as asynchronous. As co-nascent: a defiled and defiling volition is a condition for mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition. As asynchronous: a defiled and defiling volition [is a condition] for results...
The aggregates and the matter produced by them are related to [their results] by way of kamma-condition.

A defiled and corrupting state is related to both a defiled and corrupting state and a non-defiled but corrupting state by way of kamma-condition: a defiled and corrupting volition is related to its associated states...
The aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition.
A non-defiled-defiling state is a condition for a non-defiled-defiling state by way of kamma-condition:
as co-nascent and as asynchronous. As co-nascent: a non-defiled-defiling volition is a condition for its associated states...
Volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the aggregates and for the mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking ...
[etc] ... Asynchronous: unpolluted-but-polluting volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced matter.
A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement:

[this is] both conascent and asynchronous. Conascent: a volition that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates. Asynchronous: a wholesome volition that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement...
Resultant aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are related to [their concomitants] by way of kamma-condition.
A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is related to a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement by way of kamma-condition:
conascent volition that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is related to mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that is both defiled and subject to defilement, and for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement:
co-nascent volition that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a kamma-condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A resultant state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement:
one resultant aggregate that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Material phenomena are related to material phenomena by way of resultant condition …pe… two aggregates are related to two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking,

one aggregate that is neither defiled nor purifying is related to three aggregates and to the kamma-produced material phenomena by way of resultant condition …pe… two aggregates are related to two aggregates …pe… the aggregates are related to the physical basis by way of resultant condition.
A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement:
one resultant aggregate that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of resultant condition,
for three aggregates … two aggregates [are a condition] for two aggregates … [and so on].
A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement:
resultant aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are a condition, by way of resultant condition, for mind-produced matter.
A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement [is a condition] for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement and for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement...
And [it is] a condition for the Dhamma by way of resultant condition (*vipāka-paccaya*):

one resultant aggregate that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter; ... two aggregates ... [and so on].
Nutriment (*āhāra*).
A defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a defiled and corrupting state by way of nutriment-condition … three [instances].
A non-defiled but corrupting state is a condition for a non-defiled but corrupting state by way of nutriment-condition:
non-defiled but corrupting nutriments are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

Material phenomena are a condition for material phenomena by way of nutriment-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc. … edible food is a condition for this body by way of nutriment-condition.
A non-defiled and non-defiling state is a condition for a non-defiled and non-defiling state by way of nutriment-condition … three.
A defiled and corruptible state is a condition for a defiled and corruptible state by way of the faculty-condition … three.
A non-defiled but corruptible state is a condition for a non-defiled but corruptible state by way of the faculty-condition … [three].
Condition: Undefiled-but-faulty faculties are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of faculty condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc] ... the eye-faculty is related to eye-consciousness ... [etc] ...
the body-faculty is related to body-consciousness by way of faculty condition. The material life-faculty is related to kamma-produced matter.
Condition by way of faculty condition.
An undefiled and non-defiling state ... three.
Jhāna, etc.
A defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a defiled and corrupting state by way of the jhāna-condition, the path-condition, and the association-condition.
A defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a non-defiled but corrupting state by way of the dissociation-condition.

Condition: conascence and postnascence. Conascent: defiled and corruptible aggregates are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for mind-produced matter. Postnascent: defiled and corruptible aggregates are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for this prenascent body.
A state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling is a condition for a state that is neither-defiled-nor-defiling by way of dissociation-condition (vippayutta-paccaya):
as conascence, prenascence, and postnascence. As conascence:
neither-defiled-nor-defiling aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of dissociation-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, neither-defiled-nor-defiling...
The aggregates are related to derived matter by way of dissociation condition. The aggregates are related to the physical basis ... [and so on] ...
the physical basis is related to the aggregates by way of dissociation condition. As pre-arisen: the eye-base is related to eye-consciousness ... [and so on] ...

the body-base is related to body-consciousness by way of dissociation condition. The physical basis is related to the non-defiled-but-subject-to-defilement states ... [and so on] ... by way of dissociation condition.

[Aggregates] are related to aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Postnascent aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are related to this prenascent body by way of dissociation condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is related to a state that is defiled and subject to defilement by way of dissociation condition. Prenascent: the [heart-]base is related to the aggregates that are defiled and subject to defilement by way of dissociation condition.
A state that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that is corrupt but not subject to corruption.
By way of prenascence: the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for the aggregates (khandhā) that are neither corrupt nor subject to corruption.
A state that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that is corrupt but not subject to corruption.

Condition: conascence and postnascence. By way of conascence: undefiled and non-defiling aggregates are a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for mind-produced matter. By way of postnascence:
undefiled and non-defiling aggregates are a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for this prenascent body.

There is a defiled and defiling state that is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a defiled and defiling state: one defiled and defiling aggregate is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for three aggregates.
A defiled and defiling state is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a non-defiled and defiling state...

Condition: conascence and postnascence. By way of conascence: defiled and corruptible aggregates are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for mind-produced matter. By way of postnascence: defiled and corruptible aggregates are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for this prenascent body.
A defiled and corruptible state is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for both a defiled and corruptible state and a non-defiled but corruptible state:
one defiled and corruptible aggregate is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … two aggregates … [and so on] … [etc. … pe … .

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement (asaṅkiliṭṭha-asaṅkilesika) is a condition for a state that is not defiled but is subject to defilement (asaṅkiliṭṭha-saṅkilesika) by way of presence-condition (atthi-paccaya):
namely, conascence (sahajāta), prenascence (purejāta), postnascence (pacchājāta), nutriment (āhāra), and faculty (indriya). By way of conascence:
one aggregate that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of presence-condition.
...pe... At the moment of rebirth-linking ...pe... for non-percipient beings, one great primary element is a condition for three great primary elements by way of presence-condition ...pe...
As pre-nascence: one contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
the ear ...pe... the body ... forms ...pe... tangible objects ... one contemplates the [heart-]base as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
With the divine eye one sees a form; with the divine ear-element one hears a sound.
The visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of presence-condition.

The eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness … [and so on] … the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition for the aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement.

It is a condition by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*). Postnascent aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are a condition by way of presence-condition for this prenascent body.
Edible food is a condition by way of presence-condition for this body... [etc. ...The material life-faculty is a condition by way of presence-condition for kamma-produced matter.
A non-defiled-defiling state is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a defiled-defiling state.
As to pre-nascence: one relishes and delights in the eye; taking that as object, lust arises … pe … grief arises.
One relishes the [heart-]base … pe … the [heart-]base is a condition for the defiled-defiling aggregates.
Conditioned by way of presence condition (*atthipaccaya*).

A state that is neither-defiled-nor-impure is a condition, by way of presence condition, for a state that is undefiled and non-impure. By way of pre-existence: the physical basis (*vatthu*) is a condition, by way of presence condition, for the aggregates that are undefiled and non-impure.

A state that is neither-defiled-nor-impure is a condition, by way of presence condition, for a state that is undefiled and non-impure: one aggregate that is neither-defiled-nor-impure is a condition, by way of presence condition, for three aggregates … [and so on].

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of presence-condition (*atthi-paccaya*), for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement—namely, through co-nascence (*sahajāta*) and post-nascence (*pacchājāta*). As co-nascence: the aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for mind-produced matter. As post-nascence:
the aggregates that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement [are a condition] for the pre-nascent...
It is a condition for this body by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*).

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a state that is both defiled and subject to defilement, and for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement:
one aggregate that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement [is a condition] for three...

The aggregates and mind-produced matter are related to [the mind] by way of presence condition (*atthipaccaya*) … Non-defiled-but-faulty and non-defiled-and-non-faulty states are related to a non-defiled-but-faulty state by way of presence condition:
by way of conascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. Conascent: non-defiled-and-non-faulty...
The aggregates and the great elements are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*).
Postnascent—non-defiled and non-defiling aggregates and physical nutriment—are a condition for this body by way of presence-condition.
Postnascent—non-defiled but defiling aggregates and the material life-faculty—are a condition for kamma-born matter by way of presence-condition.

States that are neither corrupt nor subject to corruption and states that are not corrupt but subject to corruption are related to a state that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption by way of presence condition (*atthipaccaya*): namely, conascence (*sahajāta*) and prenascence (*purejāta*). As for conascence:
one aggregate that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption, together with the [heart-]base, is related to the three aggregates by way of presence condition …pe… (and so on).
Defiled and corrupting states and undefiled but corrupting states are related to a defiled and corrupting state by way of presence condition: conascence and prenascence. By way of conascence:
one defiled and corrupting aggregate and the [heart-]base are related to three aggregates by way of presence condition; two aggregates ... [and so on].
Defiled-and-defiling states and non-defiled-but-defiling states are related to a non-defiled-but-defiling state by way of presence condition:
as conascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. As conascence:

defiled-and-defiling aggregates and great primaries are related to mind-produced matter by way of presence condition. As post-nascence: defiled-and-defiling... [states]... are related... by way of presence condition.
The aggregates and edible food are related to this pre-arisen body by way of the presence condition.
Post-arisen defiled and defiling aggregates and the material life-faculty are related to the kamma-produced matter by way of the presence condition.
Non-existence, absence, and non-disappearance [conditions].
A defiled and corrupting state is a condition for a defiled and corrupting state by way of the absence condition … by way of the disappearance condition … by way of the non-disappearance condition.
Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.
With respect to cause, there are seven; with respect to object, six; with respect to predominance, eight; with respect to proximity, seven; with respect to contiguity, seven;
with respect to conascence, nine; with respect to mutuality, three; with respect to dependence, thirteen; with respect to strong-dependence, eight; with respect to prenascence, three;

with respect to postnascence, three; with respect to repetition, three; with respect to kamma, seven; with respect to result, four; with respect to nutriment, seven; with respect to faculty, seven; with respect to jhāna...
Seven with root, seven with path, three with association, five with dissociation, thirteen with presence, seven with absence,
seven with disappearance, and thirteen with non-disappearance.
This is the category of root-cause (hetusabhāga).
With root condition as the basis: four with predominance, seven with conascence, three with mutuality, seven with dependence, four with resultant,
four with faculty, four with path, three with association, three with dissociation, seven with presence,
and seven with non-disappearance.

Combinations based on the commonality of the root cause (*hetu-sāmañña-ghaṭanā*): Seven combinations: root, co-nascent, support, presence, and non-disappearance. Three combinations: root, co-nascent, mutuality, support, presence, and non-disappearance.
Three combinations: root, co-nascent, mutuality, support, association, presence, and non-disappearance.
Three: root, conascent, dependence, dissociation, presence, non-disappearance.

[Non-resultant—4] Four: root, conascent, dependence, resultant, presence, non-disappearance. Two: root, conascent, mutuality, dependence, resultant, presence, non-disappearance. [Root, conascent, mutuality, dependence, resultant, association, presence...]
"Non-disappearance": two. "Root, conascence, dependence, resultant, dissociation, presence, non-disappearance": two.
"Root, conascence, mutuality, dependence, resultant, dissociation, presence, non-disappearance": one. [With Resultant—5] (Abbreviated.
As in the Wholesome Triplet, so it should be expanded in detail.
Positive Order.
Negative-Exclusion:

A defiled and defiling state is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a defiled and defiling state; it is a condition, by way of co-nascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*); and it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*).
A defiled and defiling state is a condition for a non-defiled but defiling state by way of object-condition,
conascence-condition, decisive-support-condition, postnascence-condition, and kamma-condition.
A defiled and corruptible state is a condition for a non-defiled and non-corruptible state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A defiled and corruptible state is a condition for both a defiled and corruptible state and a non-defiled and non-corruptible state by way of co-nascence condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*).
A non-defiled and corruptible state is a condition for a non-defiled and non-corruptible state by way of object condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).
Conditioned by way of condition: ... conditioned by way of co-nascence condition ... conditioned by way of decisive support condition ... conditioned by way of prenascence condition ...
conditioned by way of postnascence condition ... conditioned by way of kamma condition ... conditioned by way of nutriment condition ... conditioned by way of faculty condition.

A state that is not corrupt but subject to corruption is a condition for a state that is both corrupt and subject to corruption by way of object-condition … by way of decisive support-condition … by way of prenascence-condition.

A state that is not corrupt but subject to corruption is a condition for a state that is neither corrupt nor subject to corruption by way of decisive support-condition … by way of prenascence-condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement by way of co-nascence condition … by way of decisive support condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement is a condition for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement by way of object condition … by way of co-nascence condition … by way of decisive support condition … by way of postnascence condition.

A state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement (asaṅkiliṭṭha-asaṅkilesika) is a condition, by way of co-nascence (sahajāta-paccaya), for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement (asaṅkiliṭṭha-saṅkilesika) and for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement.

States that are both undefiled but subject to defilement and neither defiled nor subject to defilement are conditions, by way of co-nascence, post-nascence (pacchājāta), nutriment (āhāra), and faculty (indriya), for a state that is undefiled but subject to defilement.

States that are both undefiled but subject to defilement and neither defiled nor subject to defilement are conditions, by way of co-nascence and pre-nascence (purejāta), for a state that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement.
Corrupt and corrupting states and non-corrupt but corrupting states are related to a corrupt and corrupting state by way of conascence and prenascence.
Corrupt and corrupting states and non-corrupt but corrupting states are related to a non-corrupt but corrupting state by way of conascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty.
1.6.7.2. Negative Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīya)
In the pure [classification], there are fourteen by way of not-root, fourteen by way of not-object, fourteen by way of not-predominance, fourteen by way of not-proximity,
fourteen by way of not-contiguity, ten by way of not-coexistence, ten by way of not-mutuality, ten by way of not-dependence, and thirteen by way of not-strong-dependence.

In the absence of pre-existence, there are twelve; in the absence of post-existence, fourteen; in the absence of repetition, fourteen; in the absence of kamma, fourteen; in the absence of result, fourteen;
in the absence of nutriment, fourteen; in the absence of faculty, fourteen;

in the absence of jhāna, fourteen; in the absence of path, fourteen; in the absence of association, ten; in the absence of dissociation, eight; in the absence of presence, eight; in the absence of absence, fourteen; in the absence of disappearance, fourteen; in the absence of non-disappearance, eight.
Under the condition of non-root (na-hetu-paccaya), there are fourteen [instances] for the non-object (na-ārammaṇa) condition. (Abbreviated.
It should be counted in the same way as the negative enumeration in the Wholesome Triplet (kusalattika).

The Dyad of Roots (Hetuduka).
With root condition, there are seven [instances] not-object; seven not-predominance; seven not-proximity; seven not-contiguity;
three not-mutuality; seven not-strong-dependence; seven not-prenascence; seven not-postnascence; seven not-repetition;
seven not-kamma; seven not-resultant; seven not-nutriment; seven not-faculty; seven not-jhāna.

Seven with root, seven with object, seven with predominance, seven with proximity, seven with contiguity, seven with conascence, seven with mutuality, seven with dependence, seven with strong-dependence, seven with prenascence, seven with postnascence, seven with repetition, seven with kamma, seven with resultant, seven with nutriment, seven with faculty, seven with jhāna, seven with path, seven with association, three with dissociation, three with presence, seven with absence, seven with disappearance, seven with non-disappearance.
Combination:

With root, conascence, dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions—there are seven in the "not-object" relation … pe … three in the "not-mutuality" relation … pe … three in the "not-association" relation, three in the "not-dissociation" relation … pe … seven in the "not-disappearance" relation. In the "Not-root" dyad: with the not-root condition, there are six [types] in the object, eight in the predominance, seven in the proximity, seven in the contiguity,
nine in the conascence, three in the mutuality, thirteen in the support, eight in the decisive support, three in the prenascence, and [three] in the postnascence.
Three in repetition; three in habituation; seven in kamma; four in result; seven in nutriment; seven in faculty; seven in jhāna; seven in path;
three in association; five in dissociation; thirteen in presence; seven in absence;
seven in disappearance; thirteen in non-disappearance.
With the root condition excluded and the object condition excluded, there are seven [instances] for the predominance condition. (Abbreviated.
